eventMetadata.context_description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom leads trader consensus as the 2028 Democratic presidential nominee at 27.3% implied probability on Polymarket, buoyed by his high-profile clashes with the Trump administration, robust national fundraising, and executive experience in the nation's largest state—differentiators over Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's progressive grassroots appeal (8.3%) and former Vice President Kamala Harris's vice-presidential tenure amid 2024 election fallout (6.5%). Recent polls, including a McLaughlin survey from early April showing Harris at 29% nationally, diverge from market pricing, where traders prioritize electability in swing states and general-election viability. Sen. Jon Ossoff (6.3%) gains from youth appeal, while the fragmented field—dozens under 5%—signals uncertainty. Consolidation could stem from 2026 midterm outcomes for governors like Newsom, key endorsements, or DNC rules favoring early frontrunners ahead of Iowa caucuses and primaries starting in 2028.

title: Fed decision in April?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's April 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for April 28-29, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their April meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Stalled US-Iran direct talks in Islamabad on April 12, mediated by Pakistan after 21 hours of marathon negotiations led by Vice President JD Vance, ended without agreement due to irreconcilable differences on nuclear restrictions, sanctions relief, and Strait of Hormuz transit protocols amid an ongoing US naval blockade of Iranian ports. The two-week ceasefire, initiated around April 7 following US and Israeli strikes that neutralized key Iranian military assets including air defenses and petrochemical facilities, faces expiration without extension, as President Trump deemed it unlikely. Iran declared no plans for further rounds post-US seizure of an Iranian-flagged vessel near the strait, while Tehran rallied pro-government support. These tensions underscore persistent diplomatic deadlock despite mutual interest in de-escalation, with indirect channels via Pakistan potentially pivotal ahead of any escalation.

Atlanta Hawks now host Game 3 on April 23 at State Farm Arena, aiming to leverage home-court advantage and even the series amid frontcourt challenges: Jock Landale remains out with a high ankle sprain, while Onyeka Okongwu is questionable due to right knee inflammation. Knicks counter with absences of Josh Hart (right ankle sprain) and Mitchell Robinson (left ankle management), straining depth. Recent regular-season head-to-heads favored New York, underscoring a tightly contested matchup shaped by injury reports and momentum shifts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Cleveland Cavaliers lead the Eastern Conference first-round playoff series 1-0 after a dominant 126-113 Game 1 win at Rocket Arena, where Donovan Mitchell scored 32 points amid efficient shooting and rebounding edges. Toronto Raptors point guard Immanuel Quickley remains out with a right hamstring sprain, depleting their backcourt depth as seen in official injury reports ahead of Game 2. With the series shifting to Scotiabank Arena for Game 3 on April 23, Raptors gain home-court advantage and crowd support, but Cleveland's stronger regular-season mark (52-30 vs. 46-36), recent 6-4 head-to-head edge, and momentum shape trader consensus toward the higher seed despite road travel. Key watch: Raptors' adjustments without Quickley and Cavs forward Thomas Bryant's absence.

eventMetadata.context_description: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. leads Polymarket odds for the 2028 Republican presidential nominee at 49%, propelled by his recent House committee testimonies defending Trump administration health reforms and advancing the Make America Healthy Again agenda against big pharma and food lobbies, resonating with populist voters. Vice President J.D. Vance trails closely at 39%, bolstered by topping the CPAC straw poll and as heir apparent to Trump's MAGA base amid his ambiguous signals on a 2028 run. Secretary of State Marco Rubio holds third at 20% on establishment appeal. This tight race reflects an open primary field after Trump's second-term ineligibility under the 22nd Amendment, with trader consensus split on continuity versus health-policy insurgency; separation could arise from Vance clarifying intentions, RFK Jr. formally joining the GOP, 2026 midterm outcomes, or early fundraising and endorsements.

eventMetadata.context_description: Finland's "Liekinheitin" by violin virtuoso Linda Lampenius and Pete Parkkonen has solidified its frontrunner status in Eurovision 2026 betting markets, commanding a trader-implied 36.7% win probability after dominating national selection buzz and early previews since its March UMK reveal. The high-energy track with live instrumentation appeals to both jury voters and televote potential, echoing Finland's 2023 success while topping OGAE fan polls and casual viewer reactions at recent pre-parties. France's Monroe with "Look!" (11.6%) and Denmark's Søren Torpegaard Lund (10.2%) trail as jury favorites, bolstered by strong staging previews, while Australia's Delta Goodrem and Greece/Israel entries gain televote traction. With Vienna rehearsals underway ahead of May semis, live performances could shift this crowded field.
